producer_report.summary: The send-back flagged one failing target, `athena-cli --test retry`. It passed on re-run (28 of 28) with no code change, so I think the failure was flaky or caused by load. The change itself is as before: `failure_section` now recognises cleanup text by content, and log tails reduce to the failing units' own output. It also adds a trailing note when no failing section is found. `CheckFailure::of` now cuts stored output with `failure_section`. The CHANGELOG entry and the new tests are in place.

checks_run.note: The target Athena flagged. All 28 tests passed on re-run with no code change. The earlier failure looks like a flaky or load-related timing issue, because retry tests start processes and the run takes 57s.

criteria_check.criterion: A new unit test in crates/athena-core/src/checks.rs feeds failure_section the log shape seen in the failed jobs (a shard log with no runner marker or ##[error], ending in the git credential-removal lines, 'Cleaning up orphan processes' and a '##[warning]Node.js 20' line, with the 'Post job cleanup.' header absent) and asserts the result contains none of those lines. It fails on the base tree and passes with the change; run `cargo test -p athena-core failure_section`.
criteria_check.evidence: Done in the earlier run. This send-back changed no code. I did not re-run the targeted test.

criteria_check.criterion: A new test in crates/athena-core/src/gh/client.rs calls detail_from_job_logs with a cancelled shard whose log has only progress lines then cleanup, and asserts output_tail holds the progress lines and a note that no failing test section was found, with no cleanup text; it also asserts a shard log with a `failures:` section still keeps the test name and panicked line. Run `cargo test -p athena-core detail_from_job_logs`.
criteria_check.evidence: Done in the earlier run: detail_tests module in gh/client.rs. No change this round.

criteria_check.criterion: A test over the stored path (with_failure_detail, plus a locally run failed check via the checks.rs run path) asserts the stored output_tail and the send_back CheckFailure tail never contain the cleanup lines, so the fix holds for every producer of a failed check record and not one job. Run `cargo test -p athena-core with_failure_detail`.
criteria_check.evidence: Done in the earlier run: tests in checks.rs, send_back.rs and routing.rs. No change this round.

criteria_check.criterion: A reading of the diff in crates/athena-core/src/checks.rs shows the cleanup recognition (is_cleanup_line or a successor) lives in one function used by the local run, the reused-CI detail and the per-shard log paths; no second copy is added in gh/client.rs or send_back.rs.
criteria_check.evidence: Recognition is only in checks.rs. client.rs and send_back.rs call failure_section, has_failing_section and no_test_section_note.

criteria_check.criterion: The CHANGELOG.md entry names the root cause (a log with no recognised failing section fell through to a plain tail of cleanup text) and what the record stores instead, and states only what the diff does.
criteria_check.evidence: The Fixed entry was added in the earlier run. No change this round.

criteria_check.criterion: `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy` and `cargo test` pass on the final tree (recorded Athena checks on the same tree count under D115).
criteria_check.evidence: left to Athena's checks. The one failing target, athena-cli --test retry, passes on re-run (28 passed).

criteria_check.criterion: No refusal or admission rule is added or tightened: git diff shows no change to admission.rs or any gate; expected 0% of newly refused readings.
criteria_check.evidence: The diff touches only the five listed files. No admission or gate file changed.

open_issues: I could not see the full output of the earlier failing test run, only that `-p athena-cli --test retry` failed. It passes now, so I made no code change this round.
learnings: The athena-cli retry test target passed when run alone (57s). The earlier failure was likely load-related or flaky, not caused by this change.
